author: Baron Godfrey Rathbone Benson Charnwood
claims: The Second Inaugural Address is one of the chief outstanding examples of Lincoln's peculiar oratorical power.
The Second Inaugural Address uses the language of intense religious feeling more unreservedly than probably any other speech of a modern statesman.
The language of intense religious feeling in the Second Inaugural Address was natural given the occasion.
The Second Inaugural Address was delivered in the context of restoring the fabric of peaceful society in the conquered South.
Lincoln received a letter from Seward withdrawing his acceptance of office the night before his inauguration, and Lincoln persuaded Seward to withdraw the letter.
The Second Inaugural Address stated that there was less occasion for an extended address than at the first inauguration.
The Second Inaugural Address noted that four years prior, all thoughts were directed to an impending civil war, which both parties sought to avert.
The Second Inaugural Address identified one-eighth of the population as colored slaves localized in the Southern part of the Union, and that this interest was somehow the cause of the war.
The Second Inaugural Address stated that neither party expected the war's magnitude or duration.
The Second Inaugural Address was delivered at the second appearance to take the oath of the Presidential office.
